scope: Written arithmetic construction of rank-one core vertices for 1913b1 at three, by checking Sakamoto Hypothesis 3.12 and cartesian Kummer conditions. Published core-vertex existence/freeness and Macias Castillo-Sano finite-level determinant/Stark isomorphism are external. No numerical auxiliary primes, compatible all-level comparison, native root generator or final chi_CT map is claimed.

sources.sakamoto_locations: Definition 3.8 and Hypothesis 3.12, printed pages 2302-2303; Lemma 3.17, page 2304; Proposition 3.22, pages 2305-2306; Proposition 4.4 and Lemma 4.6, pages 2307-2308. These establish rank-one local groups, core vertices and relaxed freeness after the written applicability checks.
sources.tate_locations: Section 19, printed pages 43-44: Tate discriminant and Galois-equivariant multiplicative uniformization. The compatible inertia action is derived in the construction from q of valuation two, not quoted as a core-vertex conclusion.
sources.determinant_stark_locations: Definitions 2.5 and 2.16; Proposition 2.4; Theorem 2.20 and equation (2.3.8); Theorem 3.4 and Corollary 3.5. Rank-one core vertices are supplied by the separate Sakamoto application, not by rank-two admissible sets.

deduction_boundary: Actual finite-level Stark bases epsilon and 2 epsilon share every component-image/Fitting ideal but have different rootability through the fixed normalized square map. Core vertices are proved to exist using external arithmetic theorems with constructed hypotheses; their primes are not independently computed. The coefficient-level return does not assert compatible inverse-limit arithmetic transport or identify the prescribed native Cassels-Tate root generator. Full named-source scalar indispensability remains open.
